subject: general
question: Near-sightedness in humans is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Myopia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In nearsightedness (myopia)**__ the **focus point is in front of the retina,** making distant objects appear blurry.

 __
 
• Nearsightedness (myopia) is a common vision condition in which you can see objects near you clearly, but distant objects are blurry.
 
• **This condition is also called nearsightedness**.
 
• Myopia is not a very complex disability.
 
• This can be easily corrected by wearing a concave lens.
 
• **A concave lens causes parallel rays of light to diverge before they converge and focus on the retina**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **cataract **is a clouding of the normally clear lens of the eye.

 
 
• For people with cataracts, looking through a cloudy lens is like looking through a frosty or foggy window.
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia **is the gradual loss of your eye's ability to focus on nearby objects. It is a natural, often annoying part of aging.
 
 
• Presbyopia usually becomes noticeable in your early to **mid-40s and tends to get worse until age 65**.
 
 
 
• **Hypermetropia **(long vision) is where the eye is smaller than normal or the cornea is too flat, meaning that the light rays are focused behind the retina.
 
 
• Rays of light from near objects, such as the pages of a book, cannot be focused clearly by the retina.
